);

We conducted experiments on a cluster of 100
nodes. Each node was equipped with 64GB RAM
and 16 CPU cores. The network had a round-trip
latency of 1 millisecond and a bandwidth of 10
gigabits per second. We measured throughput,
latency, and fault tolerance under various failure
scenarios.
2.2 Data Flow

Consensus algorithms are fundamental to
distributed systems. They ensure that multiple
nodes agree on a single value. The Paxos algorithm
is one of the most well-known consensus protocols.
Raft is a more recent alternative that is easier to
understand and implement.
2.1 Consensus Algorithms

We have demonstrated that our distributed
consensus algorithm provides high availability and
low latency under both normal and failure

The results show that our proposed algorithm
achieves 99.9 percent availability under normal
conditions. The latency remains below 50
milliseconds for 95 percent of requests. Under
failure conditions with up to 30 percent of nodes
failing, the system continues to operate with slightly
degraded performance. The consensus protocol
converges within 200 milliseconds in all tested
scenarios.
